findings.reason: The abstract-base Example independently adds concrete, abstract and static public members and requires each to fail on TS5/TS6, while protected helpers pass. The linked conformance and single-binding cases retain checks for inherited members, separate static bindings and duplicate implementations.

The Example compares exact coverage diagnostics for local export aliases on both compilers and exempts the scalar. Linked coverage cases also distinguish warn/require/off, direct exports, ignored files and explicit invalid bindings, so an exemption cannot silently admit an undesigned callable or object.

The Example changes a required parameter to optional and requires both a signature diagnostic and a blocking gate. Linked conformance cases check parameter counts, modifiers, setters and nested public types, with equivalent aliases passing and opaque/open comparisons rejected.

The Example removes only the second concrete child test and requires its inherited promise to become unlinked. The diamond, conflicting-base and inherited-lock cases check deduplication, retained origins and protection of inherited API and promises.

The Example admits two different call arities under a memberless family and then rejects an optional-parameter mismatch and missing child evidence. Linked family cases reject direct family implementations and ordinary empty contracts; changing a family promise stales the child review.

The localized CRLF Example asserts authored tags, backgrounds, steps, tables, doc strings and mapped MDX positions. Additional parser cases reject malformed, nested and duplicate blocks and unsupported structures; parsing does not evaluate the document.

The Example asserts specific failures for invalid ids, empty sentences, absent or competing carriers and duplicate normalized Example titles. Further binding cases exercise missing contracts/members, module boundaries and duplicate ids across Gherkin and JSDoc.

The Example checks the inherited Feature carrier, a property override and an unbound assumption. The parser tests separately reject reserved unsupported enforcement tags and illegal assumption bindings while permitting ordinary labels; properties remain indexed invariants.

The diamond Example asserts one inherited rule and Example on the concrete child and separate assumption indexing. Linked cases test inherited member binding, conflicting promises, child-specific evidence and locks that retain protection after changing the authored format.

The pinned legacy comparison checks equal JSON diagnostics and unchanged recorded review bytes. Other linked cases assert Gherkin stays outside generated TypeScript and that unchanged legacy material retains its existing fingerprints.

The Example starts with a valid title link and independently makes the test skipped, todo, empty, import-broken or tagged only for another rule; each loses its Example link. Concrete-child controls prevent another implementation from supplying that link.

The Example compares outline placeholders with table-test templates and literal titles, including percent and dollar placeholders and ordinary punctuation. Assertions require template normalization without stripping meaningful literal title text.

The Example checks the same missing inherited Example link under require, warn and off. Additional cases distinguish non-property rules without Examples, exempt property rules and legacy JSDoc rules, so the policy does not change unrelated linkage checks.

The Example records current reviews and separately edits Feature context, Background, assumptions, glossary and other prose. It asserts stale fingerprints and all touched rules for affected contracts; inherited-document cases retain base material too.

The Example edits only one Example step and asserts exact touched sets: its carrier marks that rule, while other contracts sharing the file have empty sets. Shared-context mutations independently assert the all-rules fallback.

The Example compares verbatim authored Example content, linked test identities, unlinked Examples and unmatched tests after a test rename. It also checks document context is shared once in Markdown and retained in JSON rather than reconstructed from titles.

The Example explicitly excludes business dates and historical text inside cases, tables and doc strings. Positive cases assert warnings for retrospective notation in prose, descriptions and rules, with original source positions.

The Example configures a matching history pattern, suppresses or disables the settled-question diagnostic and asserts the status never reappears as history. Independent historical text on the same item still remains reportable.

The Example exercises skipped, zero and suffixed item numbers and checks authored locations, then verifies consecutive Business rules and Open questions pass. Nested lists and excluded code content do not alter the sequence.

The Example sets explicit limits around a family and concrete child containing both authored formats, asserting only exceeded contract/member/rule limits. Inherited promises are distinguished from authored counts.

The Example checks every number in singular and plural citations, including lists with unrelated trailing parenthetical text. Linked cases cover missing and ambiguous document targets and require a diagnostic for each unresolved number.

The Example requires one duplicate-type finding with all three cross-module locations, then verifies same-module repeats and distinct names do not warn. The assertion checks both the primary location and related declarations.

The Example puts a reasoned directive before one historical prose block and asserts that only its named code in that block disappears. Following blocks and other codes remain visible; Gherkin directives receive corresponding scope checks.

The Example checks unused directives, whitespace-only reasons and attempts to suppress structural diagnostics. Assertions require unused warnings and explicit format errors instead of silently accepting the directive.

The Example combines structural findings with lint warnings and checks full-check ordering, diagnostic limits and the default gate. Linked tests compare disabled lint against the pinned legacy checker and preserve existing review bytes.

The Example supplies broken tsconfig, implementations, tests, locks and review records while retaining a valid design. Lint-only succeeds without inspecting those phases, still reports malformed design syntax, and leaves the filesystem snapshot unchanged.

The Example compares parsed carrier/id/sentence tuples for multiple contracts, methods and multiline promises. The preserved legacy Cage fixture repeats that comparison for all original self-spec promises, so activation of the current spec cannot turn the conversion regression into a no-op.

The Example independently checks H1/Feature placement, one retained copy of prose, CRLF/BOM handling and a title-only Feature. Layout variants also cover documents without a title and existing localized Gherkin.

The Example compares the original Gherkin prefix and retained descriptions, unrelated tags and Open questions, while checking converted rule tuples. Existing Examples and assumptions survive alongside moved method and contract promises.

The Example snapshots active designs, code, tests, locks and reviews before migration and activation. Migration changes only draft files; normal activation keeps locks and test links and stales review material without rewriting the review record.

The linked fixtures pre-create or edit migration destinations, introduce incompatible source content and simulate a source change during preparation. They assert explicit refusals and unchanged existing files, including destination symlink sentinels.

After generating a multi-contract draft, the Example reruns migration on the same source and requires unchanged status and an identical filesystem snapshot. Separate draft-edit cases ensure repetition does not overwrite a person's work.

The Example runs dry-run twice, compares identical previews and checks the entire project snapshot remains unchanged. A subsequent real migration is compared with the previewed content, including line-ending and BOM handling.

The Example asserts the complete independent set of uses, inheritance and module-import edges, node kinds and source locations. Invalid designs and unknown focus names return unavailable graphs rather than misleading empty successes.

The Example asserts exact edge sets for depth zero, forward depth one and reverse depths one and two, plus unbounded equivalence. A separate leaf query proves module imports cannot invent contract dependencies.

The Example compares JSON across both compilers and repeated calls, checks text edge counts and exact Mermaid edges derived from node identities. The complete-graph case also snapshots all files to establish read-only output.

The Example admits an explicit installed generic class and independently rejects changed class arguments, added or overridden project members and authored signature drift on both compilers. Project subclasses, structural lookalikes and wrong class identities are separate negative controls.

The Example inspects the designated project alias in the review packet. Linked vocabulary cases exercise exact named allowlists, selected initializer dependencies despite zero ordinary bounds, and refusal of runtime, undesignated or unavailable project imports.

The Example uses an external node_modules link and changes the selected declaration after recording, requiring a stale review. Linked compiler-matrix fixtures retain alias/routing/global contributions and distinguish skipLibCheck recovery from syntax errors, unresolved direct imports and forbidden project dependencies.

The Example asserts explicit skip/todo and suite-level skips retain linkage with inactive statuses and no inactive-test warning. Linked import and adapter cases independently reject broken imports and unmarked empty tests, while report assertions distinguish linked, active and unexecuted counts.

The Example creates a duplicate invariant and requires exit 1 with its exact diagnostic. Linked CLI cases assert usage/configuration/environment exit 2 and warning-only exit 0, exercising actual command output rather than a mocked status.

The Example compares the complete duplicate-invariant diagnostic line, including contract, id and independently located source position, followed by the indented other declaration. Candidate compiler-error cases also check original draft positions and separate diagnostic text from explanatory summaries.

The Example uses real compiler mismatches on TS5/TS6 and asserts a proven shared cause is grouped while every affected location and individual JSON diagnostic remains. Distinct declaration identities and multiple or clipped mismatches remain separate.

The Example checks limits 0, 1, 3, 9 and 50 against independent group selections and omitted counts, while JSON limits raw diagnostics. Linked gate cases count only blockers and retain the full summary totals.

The Example connects overlapping changed parts into one deterministic group, preserves private changes and checks executable command arrays. Missing/unknown records remain separate and current/accepted records require no packet; CLI index tests check statuses and touched sets.

The Example compares changed and context output without changing fingerprints or touched sets and inspects complete requirements, selected implementation, affected tests and helpers. Linked compact/shared-output cases retain exact source ranges, full prior findings and separate test locations across file modes.

The Example changes only one linked test and asserts affected tests, imports and complete prior findings remain in context. Linked index cases additionally exercise evidence-dependent changes, lost coverage and conservative attribution when non-test material or unexplained fingerprints change.

The Example follows a dependency symlink outside the root under both review policies and asserts its sentinel never enters packets, fingerprints or records, with no scope-limit diagnostic. Separate unreadable in-scope cases still require environment errors and refusal to record.

The Example makes an in-scope dependency unreadable and requires an incomplete packet, recording refusal and byte-identical existing records. Linked submission cases reject stale fingerprints, unknown contracts/invariants, omitted assessments and blank reasons/evidence without partial writes.

The Example records an inherited package-instance contract, edits only its family promise and requires a stale-review diagnostic. Linked mutation cases separately change designs, implementations, tests and selected dependencies and assert the named changed parts.

The Example compares declaration digests after ordinary spacing and significant compiler directives. Linked code-normalization tests distinguish inert comments from syntax, literals, annotations, ASI-sensitive changes and directive attachment while retaining authored text in packets.

The Example constructs legacy reviews and acceptances and checks current status and unchanged record bytes. Source-text edits stale legacy records; only a fresh verdict switches to the versioned fingerprint that ignores subsequent ordinary comments.

The Example changes the selected object field and a referenced initializer and requires different fingerprints on TS5/TS6. Related member cases retain called siblings, helpers and shared mutable captures instead of dropping relevant transitive behavior.

The Example changes only an independent sibling field and requires an identical fingerprint on both compilers. Related method and multi-root cases check private imports and local bindings do not make unrelated selections contaminate one another.

The Example retains nested-state mutators and escaped state and asserts their changes affect the fingerprint. Linked getter, spread, dynamic-use and observable-initializer cases require conservative whole-object or whole-file selection when independence cannot be established.

The Example explicitly invokes acceptance, inspects empty findings and acceptance flags, and asserts separate accepted/reviewed counts and a passing gate. Repeated acceptance preserves record bytes, while later material changes invalidate the corresponding acceptance.

The Example combines true blockers with coverage, scope and weak-review warnings and checks only blockers appear, including the third-block release report. Removing the blockers yields exit 0; require/warn review policy controls which review findings block.

The Example records an extendable package-instance lock and removes only the comparison marker, requiring a lock violation. Linked final/extendable and base-revision cases protect existing signatures and invariants while permitting only the documented additions.

The Example asserts CLI output equals the complete legend, with one line per code, and rejects unsupported options. The separately linked Codes contract checks the emitted-source and reference inventories in both directions.

The Example executes generated hooks through a real shell with special-character paths and compares exact arguments, absence of substitution markers and decoded TOML. Linked initialization cases preserve authored files and unrelated hooks and assert idempotent reruns.

The Example compares full check, gate, lock and review outputs and stored bytes before and after valid or malformed drafts under broad patterns. Related candidate cases reject imports of drafts and prevent another unselected draft from supplying declarations.

The Example independently computes the base digest and checks copied content, the strict header and unchanged active design. Linked creation cases cover null baselines, scaffolds, existing destinations, malformed headers, path escapes and symlinks with snapshots.

The Example resolves a consumer import through the candidate target before that target exists and rejects importing a different draft. Compiler-backed cases assert authored draft positions, unchanged snapshots and reports that explicitly leave implementations, tests and reviews unchecked.

The Example checks default candidate lint warnings, promoted error refusal with unchanged files and disabled lint reporting. It verifies the draft replaces the target for lint rather than being checked as an additional active design.

The Example omits unrelated lint and suppression errors from candidate validation while retaining structural consumer failures. Related cases keep findings involving the candidate through duplicate declarations, rule references and aggregate module limits, even when the primary location is elsewhere.

The Example asserts exact header-free target bytes, removal of the consumed draft and unchanged lock/review records. Linked refusal cases change the live target, candidate, configuration or protected declarations and require unchanged files; extendable additions remain unrecorded until an explicit lock command.

The linked Example derives diagnostic code literals from source and compares that inventory bidirectionally with the legend and reference table. It asserts one formatted line with a meaning and remedy for each code, catching both missing entries and undocumented extras.

The Example overrides only selected fields and dependency depth, asserting all other defaults remain, including maxFiles and excludes. The no-file case compares the complete default object; linked examples/lint configuration cases check their added defaults.

The Example supplies malformed JSON, invalid top-level values, wrong types and unknown fields, requiring E_CONFIG for each problem and the complete defaults on failure. Linked vocabulary, examples-policy and lint cases validate their nested keys, limits, severities and patterns.
